## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Restore the defaults resource before merge because its deletion makes every call to `load_defaults()` fail.

## Changes
The pull request adds millisecond timeout parsing, port validation, configuration loading, and host normalization, with accompanying tests and reviewer fixtures. It also deletes the bundled defaults file.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Restore the resource required by load_defaults — Calling `load_defaults()` now raises `FileNotFoundError` because you delete its required resource; `app/startup.py:6` still reads that exact file without a fallback. — Callers can no longer load the bundled timeout defaults.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — Accept port 65535 — Passing `65535` returns `False`, although your documented range includes it; the strict upper comparison excludes that valid endpoint. — Users configuring TCP port 65535 receive an incorrect validation failure.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — Expose configuration loading failures — Passing a missing file or malformed JSON returns `{}` because you catch every `Exception` without logging or signaling failure. Your docstring does not explain this fallback. — Callers cannot distinguish a failed configuration load from a successfully loaded empty object.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — Cover trailing-dot normalization — For `"Example.COM."`, your new suffix-removal branch has no test coverage; the only host test uses `"Example.COM"` and never enters it. — Removing or breaking trailing-dot stripping would leave the current host-normalization test passing. — Fix: Extend `test_normalize_host_lowercases` with a trailing-dot case.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — Align the empty-host documentation and return value — For `normalize_host("")`, your docstring promises “returns None when h is empty,” but the implementation executes `return ""`. — Callers following the documented contract cannot reliably detect empty hosts with an `is None` check. — Fix: Choose the intended empty-host result and align the documentation and implementation.
